title: ScrapingBee Pricing 2026: Plans and Credit Costs
summary: ScrapingBee pricing varies by plan, but plan costs hide what you'll actually pay per scrape. Compare all tiers to see real expenses.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


The cost check leaves a few billing questions open, and each one affects how much risk you take on before you pay.


### Is there a free plan?


Does ScrapingBee have a free plan? It has a free trial, not an ongoing free tier. You get a one-time batch of credits to test with, so use them on your hardest target pages with JavaScript rendering and proxies switched on.


If you test only easy pages, you'll underestimate your credits per successful page and pick a plan that runs out early.


### Are failed requests charged?


Are failed ScrapingBee requests charged credits? A page that loads but contains a block notice or an empty shell can still count as a success, so it can still cost credits.


Log the content of what comes back, not just the status code, and count only usable pages when you work out your real per-page cost.


### Can you change plans mid-month?


Can I change my ScrapingBee plan mid-month? Yes, plan changes are made from your account dashboard. How the credits and billing date carry over is something to read on the confirmation screen before you accept.


Treat the first month as a measurement period: if usage is clearly above or below what you bought, move once, using the measured number, and not a guess.


### Is annual billing discounted?


Does ScrapingBee discount annual billing? The catch is that you commit to a year before you know your multiplier on the sites you scrape.


Run at least one full month on monthly billing first. Switch to annual only when your credits per successful page have stopped moving.


### Is ScrapingBee cheaper than building my own scraper?


At small and moderate volume it usually is. You're not paying for proxy pools, headless browser servers, or the hours spent fixing a scraper every time a target changes its layout. Those hours are the cost most people leave out.


When volume is high and steady, the targets are few and stable, and someone on your team will own the maintenance, building your own starts to make sense. If any of those is missing, the credit multiplier is the cheaper problem to have.
